entries.name: Appium
entries.use_for: Automate iOS, Android and desktop app tests with the WebDriver protocol.
entries.why: Standard open-source mobile test automation (~22k stars), clients in many languages.
entries.summary: Open-source WebDriver-based automation framework for native, hybrid, mobile web and desktop apps. Modular with drivers, clients in many languages and plugins.
entries.best_for: Cross-platform mobile app testing on iOS and Android with your language of choice.
entries.not_for: Slower and more complex to set up than in-framework tools; device/emulator infrastructure required. Not for web-only testing.

entries.name: AVA
entries.use_for: Run Node.js tests concurrently with a minimal API.
entries.why: Lean, concurrent test runner with isolated test files; good for libraries.
entries.summary: Node.js test runner with a concise API, concurrent test execution and process isolation per file.
entries.best_for: Libraries and Node projects wanting fast, minimal tests.
entries.not_for: Node only; smaller ecosystem than Jest or Vitest, and no built-in browser or DOM environment.

entries.name: axe-core
entries.use_for: Automated accessibility (WCAG) testing of web pages and HTML UIs.
entries.why: The standard accessibility engine; many audit tools and MCP servers are built on it.
entries.summary: Accessibility testing engine for websites and HTML-based UIs. Runs in the browser or in any test setup (Playwright, Puppeteer, Selenium, Jest) and reports WCAG violations with rule ids and affected nodes.
entries.best_for: Automated WCAG checks inside your own tests, audit tools or agent workflows.
entries.not_for: Full compliance on its own: automated rules catch only part of WCAG, so manual testing is still needed.

entries.name: Capybara
entries.use_for: Acceptance tests for Ruby web apps by simulating users
entries.why: The standard browser-level testing DSL for Rails apps.
entries.summary: Ruby acceptance-testing library that simulates how a user interacts with a web app. Driver-agnostic, with Rack::Test and Selenium support and no setup for Rails.
entries.best_for: Feature and system tests for Rails and Rack apps.
entries.not_for: Ruby only; browser tests are slower than unit tests, and WebKit needs an external gem.

entries.name: Catch2
entries.use_for: Modern C++ unit, TDD and BDD testing
entries.why: Popular C++ test framework with natural test names and built-in microbenchmarks.
entries.summary: C++ unit testing framework with natural test names, assertions written as C++ expressions, sections, BDD macros and micro-benchmarking.
entries.best_for: C++ projects wanting simple, expressive tests.
entries.not_for: C++ only; compile times are heavier than doctest, and it is not a mocking framework.

entries.name: Cypress
entries.use_for: Write end-to-end and component tests that run in the browser with time-travel debugging.
entries.why: Very popular E2E tool with an interactive runner; strong developer experience.
entries.summary: Cypress is a testing tool for anything that runs in a browser, installed as an npm dev dependency on Mac, Linux or Windows. It is MIT licensed, and the optional Cypress Cloud shows test status and counts.
entries.best_for: End-to-end and component testing of web applications in a real browser from a JavaScript project.
entries.not_for: Non-browser testing such as native mobile apps or backend unit tests. Cypress Cloud is a separate hosted service.

entries.name: doctest
entries.use_for: Write fast-compiling unit tests in C++ with a single header.
entries.why: Fastest-compiling feature-rich C++ test framework; tests can live next to production code.
entries.summary: Single-header C++ testing framework that compiles very fast, designed so tests can live inside production code.
entries.best_for: C++ projects prioritizing quick compile times and in-code tests.
entries.not_for: C++ only; smaller feature set than Catch2 or GoogleTest, and no mocking.

entries.name: fast-check
entries.use_for: Add property-based tests that generate inputs and shrink failures in JS/TS.
entries.why: The standard property-based testing library for JS; works with Jest, Vitest and others.
entries.summary: Property-based testing library for JavaScript and TypeScript that generates random inputs and shrinks failures. Works with Jest, Vitest and others.
entries.best_for: Finding edge cases in pure functions and parsers.
entries.not_for: Needs well-defined properties; not a test runner and takes time to learn.

entries.name: GoogleTest
entries.use_for: Unit testing and mocking for C++
entries.why: The most widely used C++ test framework, with gMock included.
entries.summary: Google's C++ unit testing and mocking framework with xUnit-style tests, automatic test discovery, rich assertions and gMock included.
entries.best_for: C++ projects needing a standard test and mock framework.
entries.not_for: C++ only; heavier to build than header-only alternatives and macro-heavy.

entries.name: Hypothesis
entries.use_for: Find edge-case bugs in Python with property-based tests that generate inputs.
entries.why: The leading Python property-based testing library (~9k stars, MPL-2.0).

license_verified.note: LICENSE.txt: all code MPL-2.0 unless noted

entries.summary: Property-based testing library for Python. You describe input ranges via strategies, and Hypothesis generates cases, including edge cases, and shrinks failures.
entries.best_for: Finding edge-case bugs in Python code.
entries.not_for: Python only (other languages have separate implementations); needs property thinking and can slow suites.

entries.name: Jasmine
entries.use_for: BDD-style JavaScript testing for browsers and Node
entries.why: Long-standing JS test framework, still the default in many Angular projects.
entries.summary: Behavior-driven development testing framework for JavaScript that runs in browsers and Node without depending on a DOM or other framework.
entries.best_for: JS projects needing BDD-style specs, especially Angular apps that use it by default.
entries.not_for: Fewer built-ins than Jest (snapshots, module mocking); smaller community today.

entries.name: Jest
entries.use_for: Write unit tests with built-in mocking, snapshots and coverage.
entries.why: The long-time standard JS test framework (45k stars, 1.7k contributors).
entries.summary: JavaScript test framework with built-in mocking, snapshot testing, coverage and a watch mode that runs only related tests.
entries.best_for: Unit and integration tests in JS/TS projects, including React.
entries.not_for: Slow startup versus Vitest on large suites; ESM support is less seamless; not for browser E2E.

entries.name: k6
entries.use_for: Load-test APIs and websites with test scripts written in JavaScript.
entries.why: Grafana's popular load-testing tool (~32k stars, AGPL-3.0); CI-friendly with thresholds.
entries.summary: Load-testing tool where tests are scripted in JavaScript. Supports configurable load, tests as code, thresholds and CI integration.
entries.best_for: Performance and load testing of APIs and sites in CI.
entries.not_for: Scripts run in a Go runtime, not Node, so npm modules are limited; AGPL-3.0; not a functional UI test tool.

entries.name: Karate
entries.use_for: Write API, UI, mock and performance tests in a readable DSL.
entries.why: Combines API testing, mocks and perf testing in one tool, no Java code required.
entries.summary: Open-source framework combining API testing, mocks, performance testing and UI automation in a readable DSL without writing Java code.
entries.best_for: Teams wanting API and integration tests written by QA without coding.
entries.not_for: JVM-based; the DSL differs from standard programming languages; v2 is under development with migration notes.

entries.name: Keploy
entries.use_for: Generate API and integration tests by recording real traffic
entries.why: Records calls and dependencies via eBPF to produce replayable tests and mocks.
entries.summary: API and integration testing tool that records API calls, database queries and streaming events, then replays them as tests and mocks. Uses eBPF to capture traffic at the network layer, code-less and language-agnostic.
entries.best_for: Generating regression tests from real traffic for backend services.
entries.not_for: Linux/eBPF-based capture setup; replayed tests only cover recorded behavior, and complex nondeterminism needs care.

entries.name: Midscene.js
entries.use_for: Automate and test web, Android and iOS UIs with natural-language instructions.
entries.why: AI-driven UI automation from ByteDance; integrates with Playwright and Puppeteer.
entries.summary: AI-driven UI automation and testing for web, Android and iOS using natural-language instructions and vision models. Integrates with Playwright and Puppeteer.
entries.best_for: Natural-language E2E tests and visual checks, including canvas and native apps.
entries.not_for: Needs a vision-capable LLM (cost, latency, nondeterminism); less deterministic than selector-based tests.

entries.name: Mocha
entries.use_for: Run unit and integration tests in Node.js or the browser with a flexible runner.
entries.why: Long-standing JS test runner (~13M weekly npm downloads); pairs with any assertion library.
entries.summary: Flexible JavaScript test runner for Node.js and the browser. Pairs with any assertion library.
entries.best_for: Node or browser tests where you pick your own assertions and mocks.
entries.not_for: Minimal built-ins: no assertions, mocking or snapshots included; Jest or Vitest bundle more.

entries.name: Mock Service Worker
entries.use_for: Mock REST and GraphQL APIs at the network level in tests, browser and Node.
entries.why: Leading API mocking library (~23M weekly npm downloads); same mocks for tests and dev.
entries.summary: Intercepts requests at the network level (Service Worker in the browser, request interception in Node) and answers them with mocks defined using Express-like route handlers. Supports REST and GraphQL, with status codes, headers, cookies, delays and custom resolvers.
entries.best_for: Mocking APIs for unit, integration and E2E tests and for local development with the same handlers, without changing app code. Works for frontend and Node projects calling REST or GraphQL.
entries.not_for: Not a mock-server product or a general test runner. Mocks live in your JS/TS process, so it does not help non-JavaScript clients, and it does not replace contract testing against a real backend.

entries.name: Mockery
entries.use_for: Flexible mock objects for PHP tests
entries.why: Standard PHP mocking library used with PHPUnit and Pest.
entries.summary: PHP mock object framework with a readable DSL for defining expected calls, arguments and return values. Integrates with PHPUnit, PHPSpec or any test framework and is positioned as an alternative to PHPUnit's built-in mock objects.
entries.best_for: PHP unit tests that need expressive test doubles, partial mocks or expectations on interactions, especially in Laravel or Symfony projects using PHPUnit or Pest.
entries.not_for: PHP only, and only provides test doubles, not a test runner. If simple PHPUnit mocks or Prophecy already suffice, an extra dependency adds little.

entries.name: Mockito
entries.use_for: Mock objects for Java unit tests
entries.why: The most popular Java mocking framework.
entries.summary: Java mocking framework for creating mocks and spies, stubbing return values and verifying interactions in unit tests. Version 5 uses the inline mockmaker by default and requires Java 11; only the current major version is supported.
entries.best_for: Java and Kotlin-on-JVM unit tests with JUnit or TestNG where collaborators need stubbing and interaction verification.
entries.not_for: JVM only and not a test runner or assertion library. Projects stuck on Java 8 need an older Mockito line, and heavy mocking can make tests brittle compared to using real fakes.

entries.name: Pa11y
entries.use_for: Accessibility tests of URLs from the command line or Node.js.
entries.why: Simple, long-running a11y test runner for many URLs and CI.
entries.summary: Automated accessibility testing from the command line or Node.js: point it at a URL (or many) and get the issues back, with support for scripted actions such as logging in first.
entries.best_for: Quick a11y checks of live URLs and CI runs over many pages.
entries.not_for: Projects that need a permissive license to vendor the code (LGPL-3.0), or deep manual audits.

entries.name: Pest
entries.use_for: Expressive PHP testing built on PHPUnit
entries.why: Modern PHP test framework popular in the Laravel community.
entries.summary: PHP testing framework built on top of PHPUnit with a concise, expressive syntax and a plugin ecosystem. README itself is thin and points to pestphp.com for docs; v5 is announced and it is pitched for PHP developers and AI agents.
entries.best_for: PHP and especially Laravel projects that want readable tests with less boilerplate while keeping PHPUnit compatibility.
entries.not_for: PHP only and depends on PHPUnit underneath. Teams that prefer class-based xUnit style or want zero extra layers may stay with plain PHPUnit.

entries.name: PHPUnit
entries.use_for: Unit testing for PHP
entries.why: The standard PHP testing framework underlying Laravel, Symfony and Pest.
entries.summary: Programmer-oriented PHP testing framework following the xUnit architecture. It is the base test runner used by most PHP frameworks and tools such as Pest.
entries.best_for: Unit and integration testing in any PHP project, including Laravel and Symfony, where a standard, well-supported runner is wanted.
entries.not_for: PHP only. Syntax is more verbose than Pest; it is not for browser or E2E testing and has no built-in mocking beyond its own test doubles.

entries.name: Playwright
entries.use_for: Write reliable end-to-end tests across Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.
entries.why: Leading E2E framework (98k stars) with auto-waiting, tracing, codegen and bindings for 4 languages.
entries.summary: Browser automation and end-to-end testing framework for Chromium, Firefox and WebKit with bindings for several languages. Offers auto-waiting, tracing, codegen, and (per the README) a playwright-cli and accessibility-tree snapshots that let AI agents drive pages.
entries.best_for: Cross-browser E2E tests, web scraping and browser automation, including agent-driven browsing, in Node, Python, Java or .NET projects.
entries.not_for: Heavy for pure unit or component tests and downloads browser binaries. For simple HTTP API testing a lighter tool suffices; browsers are fixed to the bundled engines, not arbitrary real devices.

entries.name: pytest
entries.use_for: Write simple to complex Python tests with fixtures and plain asserts.
entries.why: The de facto Python test framework with 1,000+ plugins.
entries.summary: pytest is a Python testing framework that lets you write tests with plain assert statements and get detailed assertion introspection on failure. It auto-discovers test modules and functions, has modular fixtures, runs unittest suites, and has 1300+ external plugins.
entries.best_for: Unit, functional and integration testing of Python 3.10+ (or PyPy3) applications and libraries.
entries.not_for: Non-Python codebases, or browser end-to-end testing on its own (plugins are needed for that).

entries.name: React Testing Library
entries.use_for: Test React components the way users interact with them.
entries.why: Standard React component testing library (~70M weekly npm downloads).
entries.summary: Utilities for rendering React components to the DOM and querying them the way users do (by role, label, text) rather than by implementation details. Works with hooks and class components and sits on top of DOM Testing Library.
entries.best_for: Component and integration tests for React apps run under Jest or Vitest with jsdom, focused on user-visible behavior.
entries.not_for: React DOM only; it is not a test runner and does not test in a real browser or cover visual regressions. Use other Testing Library flavors for Vue or Svelte, or Playwright for E2E.

entries.name: Robot Framework
entries.use_for: Keyword-driven acceptance testing and RPA
entries.why: Mature generic automation framework with a large library ecosystem (Browser, Selenium, Appium).
entries.summary: Generic automation framework for acceptance testing, ATDD and RPA using a plain-text, keyword-driven syntax. Implemented in Python and extended through libraries such as Browser, Selenium and Appium maintained as separate projects.
entries.best_for: Acceptance and end-to-end testing by mixed technical and non-technical teams, or RPA tasks, where readable keyword-based test cases are valued.
entries.not_for: Keyword syntax is a different paradigm from code-first test frameworks and adds overhead for small unit tests. Most capabilities require installing separate libraries.

entries.name: SeleniumBase
entries.use_for: Write Python browser tests and automation on top of Selenium and pytest.
entries.why: Batteries-included Python E2E framework with recorder, dashboards and CDP mode.
entries.summary: Python framework combining Selenium, pytest and extras for browser automation, scraping and testing. Includes a recorder, dashboard, reports, UC and CDP modes with stealth options to bypass bot detection.
entries.best_for: Python teams wanting quick E2E tests or automation scripts with built-in waits, screenshots, reports, and stealth browsing for scraping.
entries.not_for: Python only and Selenium-based; Playwright may be preferable for modern multi-browser testing. Stealth and CAPTCHA-bypass features may conflict with sites' terms of use.

entries.name: Sinon.JS
entries.use_for: Add spies, stubs, mocks and fake timers to JavaScript tests.
entries.why: Standard standalone test doubles library (~11M weekly npm downloads), framework-agnostic.
entries.summary: Standalone, framework-agnostic library of test spies, stubs, mocks and fake timers for JavaScript. Avoids global pollution and embeds with any test framework.
entries.best_for: JavaScript or TypeScript tests (Mocha, Jest, Node test runner) needing spies, stubs or fake timers independent of the runner.
entries.not_for: Jest and Vitest already ship built-in mocking, so Sinon is redundant there. It does not provide a test runner, assertions or network-level request mocking.

entries.name: Testcontainers
entries.use_for: Spin up real databases and services in Docker for integration tests.
entries.why: The original Testcontainers (~9k stars); ports exist for Node, Go, Python, .NET.
entries.summary: Java library that starts throwaway Docker containers (databases, browsers, any image) for JUnit tests, giving integration tests real dependencies. Ports exist for other languages.
entries.best_for: Integration tests on JVM projects that need a real Postgres, Kafka, Redis or other service instead of mocks or in-memory substitutes.
entries.not_for: Requires a Docker-compatible runtime on dev machines and CI, and containers slow test startup versus mocks. For other languages use the matching Testcontainers port.

entries.name: testify
entries.use_for: Write Go tests with assertions, mocks and suites.
entries.why: Most-used Go testing toolkit (~26k stars).
entries.summary: Go toolkit adding assert and require packages, mocking, and test-suite helpers on top of the standard testing package. The repo is maintained at v1 with no breaking changes accepted.
entries.best_for: Go projects that want concise assertions, simple mocks and suite structure without a heavier BDD framework.
entries.not_for: Mocks are hand-written or need mockery for generation, and v1 is frozen so API changes are unlikely. Teams favouring only the stdlib or go-cmp may not need it.

entries.name: Vitest
entries.use_for: Run fast unit and component tests with a Jest-compatible API, powered by Vite.
entries.why: Default test runner for Vite projects; native ESM/TS, browser mode and fast watch.
entries.summary: Test runner built on Vite that reuses the app's Vite config and plugins. Offers a Jest-compatible API, snapshots, built-in coverage, watch mode like HMR, jsdom/happy-dom, browser mode for component tests, and TypeScript/ESM out of the box.
entries.best_for: Unit and component testing of Vite-based and modern TypeScript/ESM projects across React, Vue, Svelte and others.
entries.not_for: Requires recent Vite (6.4+) and Node (22.12+). Large legacy Jest suites may need migration effort, and it is not an E2E browser automation tool.
